title: Simple subspaces expose weak evidence for Krylov transfer
question: Does learning from Lanczos trajectories improve label efficiency for quantum ground states beyond credible simple baselines?
method: Retained synthetic development study: 16 by 16 interior grid, one training seed, twelve in distribution test potentials, and 20 labeled examples.

A joint embedding model predicts trajectory representations; the potential encoder transfers to energy and wavefunction regression. Neural values come from retained aggregates; classical means are rechecked from per-example records.
lesson: A fixed free-box state and a nine-mode Rayleigh Ritz model reveal that high overlap can be easy on a smooth distribution. Physical residuals expose errors hidden by fidelity.
result: The retained Krylov model does not establish useful transfer. Its paired fidelity interval against free box includes zero; the nine-mode comparison favors the classical baseline within this corpus.
Ritz uses the query Hamiltonian and has a different inference cost. These comparisons do not establish equal compute dominance.
limits: One training seed. Exploratory intervals exclude training seed uncertainty. The larger confirmatory experiment has not run.
source_line: Evidence: retained smoke summary and classical baseline audit. Presentation input commit 24e871d27215. Per-example baseline arithmetic is checked; no model replay or new scientific outcome is claimed.
